Date of institution : 12.07.2022 Nature of the Case : Seeking  Compensation/Award Date of commencement of : 05.02.2024 Recording of evidence Date of Judgment : 10.02.2025 pronounced  SCCH-08 3 MVC No.3636/2022  JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Shivamma, in the road traffic accident that took place on 06.12.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 06.12.2021 at about 11.15 a.m., when the deceased was proceeding by walk inside the KSRTC Bus stand, Magadi Town, Ramanagara, at that time suddenly the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-42-F-2134 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased, due to which she sustained Munirathnamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138917641/
2 injuries and on the way to the hospital, succumbed to the injuries.

Thereafter,
post-mortem was conducted at Magadi Government hospital and dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.

It is stated that the deceased was running a chicken shop and earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to her death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.

It is further contended that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending KSRTC bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-42-F-2134.
Hence, the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
3. On service of notice, respondents have appeared before the court through their counsels and filed objection statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
The respondent has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.

It has denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-42-F-2134 in the accident and contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligence of the deceased herself.
The respondent has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. The respondents No.2 to 4 in their written statement have contended that, deceased Shivamma had 3 children namely Munirathnamma, Late Venkatesh and Late Manjunath D.
Petitioner Munirathnamma is the daughter and respondent No.2 is the daughter-in-law and respondent No.3 and 4 are grand children of the deceased Shivamma.
Due to sudden death of Shivamma, her son Manjunath D. mentally shocked and committed suicide.

Petitioner has not made them as parties,
and hence through impleading application impleaded themselves as parties.
Further admitted the Column No. 1 to 3 and 6 to 21 and denied the contents of column No.4 and 5 of the petition.
It is contended that deceased was living with her son in Bengaluru and she was running chicken stall with her son in the name of Fresh Chikkan Stall and contributing entire income to their family.
Due to the demise of the deceased and her son, they have lost love and affection and also facing financial difficulties.
It is contended that petitioner is married and living separately along with her husband and children and she is not dependent on the income of the decease.
Among other grounds prays to allow the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:-

sentences.text: 1. Whether the petitioner proves that she is legal heir of deceased Smt. Shivamma?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that on 06.12.2021 at about 11.15 a.m., in Ramanagara KSRTC bus stand driver of the said bus bearing Reg. No.KA-42-F-2134 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased who was proceeding towards bus stand by walking due to which she sustained injuries and later she succumbed due to the injuries?

3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or Award?

Additional Issue 1. Whether the respondents No.2 to 4 proves that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Smt.
Shivamma?
7. In order to prove the case, petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and a witness as PW.2 and got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P1 to 13.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 examined herself as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R1 to R12 documents.
The respondent No.1 has examined one witness as RW.2.
8. Heard the arguments.

9. My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ...

In the affirmative,
 Addl. Issue No.1 ...

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 ...

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 ...

Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4 ... As per final order  For the following:
 REASONS  10. Issue No.1 & Addl. Issue No.1:
The petitioner is stated to be the daughter of the deceased Shivamma and respondents No.2 is the daughter-in-law and respondents No.3 and 4 are grand children of the deceased

To prove the same,
petitioner has filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Adhaar card and Transfer certificate produced at Ex's.P.11 and 12 do fortify the said fact.

Munirathnamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138917641/
4
It is pertinent to note that the relationship of the petitioner with the deceased has been disputed by the respondents No.2 to 4.
Respondents No.2 to 4 came on record through impleading application contending that they are the daughter-in-law and grand children of the deceased Shivamma.

The death certificate of Shivamma, Genealogical tree/pedigree, Ration cards, Birth certificates, death certificate of Manjunath D. marked at Ex.R1 to Ex.R10 and Ex.R12 fortify that, Late Manjunath D. is son of the deceased and respondents No.2 to 4 are daughter-in-law and grand children of deceased Shivamma.
It has to be noted that, respondent No.2 is the daughter-in- law of the deceased Shivamma.

Generally, a daughter-in-law is not considered a dependent on her mother-in-law's income unless there is a clear and demonstrable financial reliance where the daughter-in-law is primarily supported by the mother-in-law.

Most legal frameworks define a dependent as someone who relies primarily on another individual for financial support, usually including spouses, children, and sometimes parents, but not typically in-laws.
But in this case 2nd Respondent's husband was died after the death of the deceased Shivamma.
As per Hindu succession Act the deceased son's widow and grand children are class II legal heir of the deceased estate.
Hence this Tribunal hold that the petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4 are the legal heirs/representatives of the deceased Shivamma and dependents of deceased.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 and Additional Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
It is the case of the petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4 that, on 06.12.2021 at about 11.15 a.m., in Ramanagara KSRTC bus stand driver of the said bus bearing Reg.

No .KA-42-F-2134 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased who was proceeding towards bus stand by walk due to which she sustained injuries and later she succumbed due to the injuries.
It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the Bus driver and as such the respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation to them.

12. In order to substantiate the contentions, petitioner stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot mahazar,
Sketch, IMV Report, Inquest Report, P.M. Report and charge sheet at Ex.P1 to 8.

On the other hand,
respondent No.1 has examined its driver as RW.1.
13.
This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of Bus.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.

Munirathnamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138917641/
5
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

14. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened at Ramanagara KSRTC bus stand,
when the deceased person who was proceeding towards bus stand by walking, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-42-F-2134 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.4 Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.4 it reflects that deceased was proceeding towards bus stand by walking and suddenly the offending KSRTC bus came in a negligent manner and dashed against the deceased Shivamma.
If the driver of bus coming in a normal speed by observing ongoing passengers who were walking inside the Bus stand to reach the platforms, then he could certainly avoid the accident.

Added more the contents of Ex.P.3 and P5 which are the spot mahazer and IMV report itself discloses that accident occurred in the Bus stand and there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P8 was also filed as against the driver of the bus.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P8 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence of the bus.

15. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a Munirathnamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138917641/
6 particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case though the driver of the bus is examined as RW.2 to show that there was no negligence on his part, even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the bus and he was charge sheeted.
16. The petitioners with the help of Ex.P3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P8 clearly demonstrated that there was negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-42-F-2134 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.2 In the Affirmative.

Issue No.3:
17.

While answering issue No.2, I have already observed that the death of Shivamma, was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-42-F-2134.
18.
The petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4 have contended that the deceased and her son were running chicken stall in the name of Fresh Chicken stall and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In proof of the same, RW.1 has produced Ex.R11 for having taken permission to run the chicken stall.
But, in proof of income, not produced any documents before the court.
The accident occurred in the year 2021.

Hence, this court has taken notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- p.m..
19.
It is stated that the deceased was aged 55 years at the time of the accident.
RW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.R7 which shows the date of birth as 18.02.1964.
The accident was occurred in the year 2021.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 56 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '9'.
20.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years Munirathnamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138917641/
7 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and she died at the age of 56 years.
Therefore, in this case, 15% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Hence, 15% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.17,250/-p.m. (Rs.15,000/- +
2,250/- i.e.15%).
The deceased died leaving behind 4 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.12,938/- p.m.(Rs. 17,250- Rs.4,312).
21.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.12,938/- p.m. and the multiplier '9' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.13,97,304/- (Rs.12,938 X 12 X 9).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.13,97,304/- under the head of loss of dependency.

22. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The RW.1 contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

23. In this case, the petitioner is the daughter and respondent No.2 is the daughter-in-law,
respondent No.3 and 4 are minor grand children of the deceased.

As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium,
as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of children/father/mother as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a mother cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their mother.
Therefore, petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

24. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.13,97,304/-
 2. Towards loss to estate Rs.18,150/-
3. Towards transportation of dead Rs.18,150/- body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses 4.

Towards loss of Filial Rs.1,76,000/-
Munirathnamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 February, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138917641/
8
consortium to petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4(Each Rs.44,000/-) Total Rs.16,09,604/-

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,09,604/-.
25.
As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the petitioner is the daughter, respondents No.2 to 4 are daughter-in-law and grand children of the deceased.

Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners and respondents No.2 to 4 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of petitioner 50%, respondents No.2 to 4 at the ration of 10:20:20 respectively.
26. The petitioners are claiming interest @ 9% per annum on the compensation amount.
The respondent No.1 has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
27. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending KSRTC bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-42-F-2134.
It is not in dispute that respondent is not the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, it is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4.

Accordingly,
I answer issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4 are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,09,604/- (Rupees Sixteen lakhs nine thousand six hundred and four only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner - 50%
 Respondent No.2 - 10%
 Respondent No.3 - 20%
 Respondent No.4 - 20%
Munirathnamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138917641/
9

Out of the share amount of Petitioner and respondent No.2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names respectively in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 2 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner and respondent No.2 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor respondents No.3 and 4 is ordered to be deposited in their respective names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority, at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor respondents with liberty to the respondent No.2 to draw periodical interest.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

ISSUES Munirathnamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138917641/
3
1. Whether the petitioner proves that she is legal heir of deceased Smt. Shivamma?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that on 06.12.2021 at about 11.15 a.m., in Ramanagara KSRTC bus stand driver of the said bus bearing Reg. No.KA-42-F-2134 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased who was proceeding towards bus stand by walking due to which she sustained injuries and later she succumbed due to the injuries?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or Award?
Additional Issue 1. Whether the respondents No.2 to 4 proves that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Smt.
Shivamma?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is pertinent to note that the relationship of the petitioner with the deceased has been disputed by the respondents No.2 to 4.
Respondents No.2 to 4 came on record through impleading application contending that they are the daughter-in-law and grand children of the deceased Shivamma.
The death certificate of Shivamma, Genealogical tree/pedigree, Ration cards, Birth certificates, death certificate of Manjunath D. marked at Ex.R1 to Ex.R10 and Ex.R12 fortify that, Late Manjunath D. is son of the deceased and respondents No.2 to 4 are daughter-in-law and grand children of deceased Shivamma.
It has to be noted that, respondent No.2 is the daughter-in- law of the deceased Shivamma.
Generally, a daughter-in-law is not considered a dependent on her mother-in-law's income unless there is a clear and demonstrable financial reliance where the daughter-in-law is primarily supported by the mother-in-law.
Most legal frameworks define a dependent as someone who relies primarily on another individual for financial support, usually including spouses, children, and sometimes parents, but not typically in-laws.
But in this case 2nd Respondent's husband was died after the death of the deceased Shivamma.
As per Hindu succession Act the deceased son's widow and grand children are class II legal heir of the deceased estate.
Hence this Tribunal hold that the petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4 are the legal heirs/representatives of the deceased Shivamma and dependents of deceased.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
15. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a Munirathnamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138917641/
6 particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Even in the instant case though the driver of the bus is examined as RW.2 to show that there was no negligence on his part, even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the bus and he was charge sheeted.
16. The petitioners with the help of Ex.P3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P8 clearly demonstrated that there was negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and she died at the age of 56 years.
23. In this case, the petitioner is the daughter and respondent No.2 is the daughter-in-law,
respondent No.3 and 4 are minor grand children of the deceased.
As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium,
as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of children/father/mother as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of a mother cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their mother.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.13,97,304/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Therefore, petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
24. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.13,97,304/-
 2. Towards loss to estate Rs.18,150/-
3. Towards transportation of dead Rs.18,150/- body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses 4.
In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,09,604/-.
25.
26. The petitioners are claiming interest @ 9% per annum on the compensation amount.
Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
27. Liability:
It is not in dispute that respondent is not the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, it is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4.
Accordingly,
I answer issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.4:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioner and respondents No.2 to 4 are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,09,604/- (Rupees Sixteen lakhs nine thousand six hundred and four only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner - 50%
 Respondent No.2 - 10%
 Respondent No.3 - 20%
 Respondent No.4 - 20%

Out of the share amount of Petitioner and respondent No.2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names respectively in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 2 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner and respondent No.2 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
The share amount apportioned in the name of minor respondents No.3 and 4 is ordered to be deposited in their respective names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority, at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor respondents with liberty to the respondent No.2 to draw periodical interest.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
